predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: Persis, ruled by local Fratarakas 'subject to the' Seleucids from the end of the 3rd or the start of the 2nd century BC

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Persis, 'Incorporated into the Sasanian Empire in AD 224'; the kings' last, Ardashir V, is Ardashir I

ledger.x: c. 150 BC: Persis wins independence from the Seleucids under its frataraka Vahbarz (Wadfradad I). Fratarakas page: he 'obtained independence circa 150 BC' as Seleucid power waned; the Kings of Persis page has Strabo calling the early kings tributaries until c. 140 BC. c. 138 BC: Persis becomes a vassal of the Parthian Empire under Mithridates I. Kings of Persis page: 'Later the frataraka Wadfradad II (fl. 138 BC) was made a vassal of the Iranian Parthian (Arsacid) Empire'; Strabo, quoted on the same page: 'the early kings of Persis were tributaries to the Seleucid rulers, until…
After 132 BC: the Kings of Persis replace the Fratarakas, 'most likely at the accession of Parthian king Phraates II (r.
205/6: Pabag overthrows the Bazrangid king Gochihr and takes Istakhr, the house that becomes the Sasanians.
28 April 224: the vassalage ends when Ardashir (Ardashir V of Persis, 211/2-224) defeats Artabanus IV at Hormozdgan.
28 April 224: Ardashir defeats Artabanus IV on the Hormozdgan plain and the kingdom of Persis becomes the core of the Sasanian Empire.

wars.name: Parthian conquest of Persis
wars.outcome: Mithridates I took control of Persis but let the local rulers stay: he installed Wadfradad II as frataraka with more autonomy and made Persis a Parthian vassal.

wars.name: Ardashir's revolt against the Arsacids
wars.outcome: Ardashir, king of Persis from 211/2, subdued the neighbouring lands in defiance of Arsacid rule and on 28 April 224 defeated and killed Artabanus IV at Hormozdgan, founding the Sasanian Empire.

certainty.note: Neither page gives a boundary or an area; Persis is drawn as the region the sources name, with soft edges throughout.
